history.summary: Split follows time spent and client-driven rework: Jun spent the most time on four cuts and export, Mina wrote the script through three versions, and Sora recorded the voiceover three times.

reasons.text: Wrote the script and shaped the story and voiceover; 165 minutes over three versions.
Revised after client asked for a shorter intro and a product-shot close.
Most time on the job: four edit cuts plus export, 265 minutes.
Fixed subtitle overflow and re-synced new voiceovers after client feedback.
Recorded the voiceover and delivered the best take.
Re-recorded the full voiceover twice for a warmer tone as the client asked.

history.changedBecause: No change: Jun's dispute asks for 70% because editing is hard, which is a claim about difficulty and a demand for a number, not evidence. I checked Jun's events e07, e09, e11, e13, e14 (265 minutes) and the subtitle and re-sync work in e08, e09, e11. The v1 split already counted all of it, and Jun already has the largest share.

disputes.text: Re-recording 3 wasn't logged: after Re-recording 2 (e12) I recorded pickup lines for the closing line, and they went into the final cut (e13).
disputes.answer: Sora's dispute points at specific work: pickup lines for the closing line (e16, 22 min), recorded after Re-recording 2 (e12) and before the final cut (e13). Nothing in the log contradicts it, so I counted it. This change rests on a line Sora added (e16). Sora goes from 20% to 23%, taking 2 from Jun and 1 from Mina. Jun's dispute (70% because editing is hard) gives no new log evidence, so Jun's work (e07, e09, e11, e13, e14) stays counted as before.
